vocab.notes: Usually means a romantic partner. A friend is kamarád / kamarádka.
Plural of dítě (child). It behaves like a feminine plural: ty děti, krásné děti.
jeden rok, dva roky, pět let.

dialogue.setting: Coffee break in the office kitchen. Daniel's colleague Martina shows him a photo on her phone.

lines.speaker: Martina
lines.cs: To je moje [[rodina|rodina|nom|naming]]. To je můj [[manžel|manžel|nom|naming]] Petr a tohle jsou naše [[děti|dítě|nom.pl|naming]].
lines.en: This is my family. That's my husband Petr and these are our children.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.en: They're lovely. How old are they?

lines.speaker: Martina
lines.en: My son is seven and my daughter four.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.cs: Ne, ale mám [[přítelkyni|přítelkyně|acc|object]]. Taky je z [[Anglie|Anglie|gen|after-z]] a pracuje tady v [[Brně|Brno|loc|location-v-na]].
lines.en: No, but I have a girlfriend. She's from England too and works here in Brno.

exercises.listen: Synovi je sedm a dceři čtyři.

hints.explain: "Synovi je sedm": the son is seven; "dceři čtyři": the daughter four.

exercises.why: "Synovi je sedm a dceři čtyři." My son is seven and my daughter four. Age uses the dative: synovi, dceři.

exercises.listen: Ne, ale mám přítelkyni. Taky je z Anglie.
options: No, but he has a girlfriend from England
No, and he lives alone in Brno
answers: No, but he has a girlfriend from England

hints.explain: "Ne" is no; "přítelkyni" is girlfriend, not a daughter ("dcera").

hints.wrong: No, and he lives alone in Brno
hints.explain: He does say no, but "mám přítelkyni": he has a girlfriend.

exercises.why: "Ne, ale mám přítelkyni. Taky je z Anglie." No, but I have a girlfriend. She's from England too.
After mít, the object is in the accusative. Masculine animate nouns (people and animals) add -a: bratr → bratra.

hints.explain: -u is the accusative of feminine nouns in -a (sestru). bratr is masculine animate: bratra.

exercises.why: Feminine -a → -u in the accusative: sestra → sestru.

hints.explain: sestra is the object of mám: use the accusative, sestru.

exercises.why: Czech gives age with the dative: Je mi třicet (let), literally "It is to me thirty (years)".

hints.explain: Czech doesn't say "I am thirty". Use the dative: Je mi třicet (let).
That's how some languages say it, but Czech uses the dative: Je mi třicet let.

exercises.why: Kolik ti je (let)? literally "How many (years) is it to you?". Formal: Kolik vám je?

hints.explain: Czech uses the dative for age: Kolik ti je?
That's the formal form. Informal: Kolik ti je?

exercises.question: Which case is "mi"?
exercises.why: Age uses the dative: Je mi třicet (to me it is thirty). mi is the short dative of já.
přítelkyně usually means girlfriend (romantic partner). A female friend is kamarádka.

hints.explain: Careful: přítelkyně usually means girlfriend or partner. A (female) friend is kamarádka.

exercises.why: manžel is masculine, so "my" is můj.

hints.explain: moje / má is for feminine (and neuter) nouns. manžel is masculine: můj manžel.

exercises.why: manželka is feminine, so "my" is moje (or má).

hints.explain: můj is masculine. manželka is feminine: moje manželka.

exercises.prompt: Say no, but you have a girlfriend.
exercises.why: přítelkyně is the object of mám, so it's in the accusative: soft feminine -e → -i, přítelkyni.

hints.explain: přítelkyně is the object of mám: accusative přítelkyni (like růže → růži).
kamarádka is a (female) friend. Girlfriend is přítelkyně: mám přítelkyni.
